issues.label: Standard of review for PCR denial
issues.why: Court must determine whether abuse-of-discretion or de novo review applies to denial of the petition.

issues.label: Mootness of ineffective assistance claim
issues.why: Whether Johnson I's affirmance actually rendered the IAC claim moot given new outside-record evidence.

issues.label: Res judicata bar to PCR claims
issues.why: Whether claims that could have been raised on direct appeal are barred, as opposed to those resting on outside-record evidence.

issues.label: Entitlement to evidentiary hearing
issues.why: Whether petitioner's submissions established substantive grounds warranting a hearing under R.C. 2953.21.

issues.label: Sufficiency of supporting evidentiary materials
issues.why: Whether affidavits or new evidence dehors the record met the threshold to compel a hearing.

issues.label: Effect of miscited statute (2953.21(C))
issues.why: Whether citing the death-penalty provision defeats or is excusable in the petition.

issues.label: Timeliness of the petition
issues.why: Whether the petition was filed within statutory deadlines and jurisdictional requirements were met.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings of fact/conclusions
issues.why: Whether the trial court's entry complied with R.C. 2953.21(H) and Penland.

issues.label: Newly discovered evidence standard
issues.why: Whether the claimed new evidence qualifies and could not have been raised earlier.

issues.label: Applicability to weapons case (22CRC-I0207)
issues.why: Whether mootness reasoning from Johnson I applies to the separate no-contest conviction with no direct appeal decided.

issues.label: Remedy if findings inadequate
issues.why: Whether remand for proper findings or hearing is required versus affirmance.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance merits (Strickland)
issues.why: Whether deficient performance and prejudice were shown to warrant relief.

issues.label: Jurisdiction to consider petition during appeal
issues.why: Whether filing PCR before Johnson I decided affects the trial court's authority.
